title: Deductible Hold on the Reconstruction Final Draw
content:
The deductible hold on the final draw of a Reconstruction contract keeps out the insured's deductible, which the carrier never pays. It reads the claim file kept under Insurance Claim Services: whether its claim arrangement has the company collect the deductible, the deductible due on the claim file and the claim file's deductible amount.

**Carrier-funded.** A final draw is carrier-funded when its funding route, set by the base draw rule from the linked claim file, is not the customer: the claim file has a dwelling payment the carrier issued to the company directly (contractor direct), by a check naming the insured and the company (insured two-party), or into the mortgagee's loss-draft account (mortgagee loss draft). On any other final draw the customer funds the draw.

**Rule.** On a carrier-funded final draw:

- when the claim arrangement has the company collect the deductible and deductible is due on the claim file, the deductible due is held;
- when the claim arrangement does not have the company collect the deductible, the claim file's whole deductible amount is held, because the carrier paid net of it;
- otherwise no deductible is held.

On a final draw that is not carrier-funded no deductible is held, because the customer funds the draw.

## Combinations

| Carrier-funded | Arrangement has the company collect the deductible | Deductible due on the claim file | Deductible hold |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | an amount above zero | the deductible due |
| yes | yes | none due | none |
| yes | no | any | the whole deductible amount |
| no | any | any | none |

**Example (hypothetical).** A claim file with a $2,500.00 deductible of which $1,000.00 is still due: where the arrangement has the company collect the deductible, $1,000.00 is held; where it does not, $2,500.00 is held.
